quote_original: Here is a practical application of this theory.
context_before: Fancy assembles, imagination fuses.
context_after: A year ago, a blind girl living in the city of San Francisco found herself confronted with a transportation problem. A rerouting of buses forced her to make three transfers between her home and her office. This lengthened her trip from fifteen minutes to two hours and fifteen minutes. She thought seriously about this problem and came to the decision that a car was the solution. She knew that she could not drive a car but felt that she could be driven in one. Putting this theory to the test that âwhenever the actions of the inner self correspond to the actions which the outer, physical self must take to appease desire, that desire will be realizedâ, she said to herself, âI will sit here and imagine that I am being driven to my office.â
selection_note: Key statement from Chapter 3: Highways of the Inner World on awakened imagination, revision, and inner speech.

quote_original: Here is the way an artist friend forgave herself and was set free from pain, annoyance and unfriendliness.
context_before: All things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, even so do ye to them: for this is the law. Matthew 7:12
context_after: Knowing that nothing but forgetfulness and forgiveness will bring us to new values, she cast herself upon her imagination and escaped from the prison of her senses. She writes: âThursday, I taught all day in the art school. Only one small thing marred the day. Coming into my afternoon classroom, I discovered the janitor had left all the chairs on top of the desks after cleaning the floor. As I lifted a chair down, it slipped from my grasp and struck me a sharp blow on the instep of my right foot. I immediately examined my thoughts and found that I had criticized the man for not doing his job properly. Since he had lost his helper, I realized he probably felt he had done more than enough and it was an unwanted gift that had bounced and hit me on the foot. Looking down at my foot, I saw both my skin and nylons were intact, so forgot the whole thing.
selection_note: Key statement from Chapter 4: The Pruning Shears of Revision on awakened imagination, revision, and inner speech.
